signature: SUBROUTINE DSYTRF_AA( UPLO, N, A, LDA, IPIV, WORK, LWORK, INFO )

params.name: uplo
params.reference:
-   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
-   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference:
On entry, the symmetric matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.

On exit, the tridiagonal matrix is stored in the diagonals and the subdiagonals of A just below (or above) the diagonals, and L is stored below (or above) the subdiagonals, when `UPLO` is 'L' (or 'U').

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: IPIV
params.reference: On exit, it contains the details of the interchanges, i.e., the row and column k of A were interchanged with the row and column `IPIV(k)`.
params.workDependent: where pivot candidates tie exactly, which one is chosen depends on the rounding of the block size LWORK selects, in the reference as in the JS

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The length of `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,2 \, N)$. For optimum performance $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N \, (1+\mathrm{NB})$, where NB is the optimal blocksize.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

overrides.reason: DSYTRF_AA shrinks its block size from LWORK (NB = (LWORK-N)/N when LWORK < (1+NB)*N). The blocked and the block-size-1 runs round differently, and where two pivot candidates tie exactly in magnitude (the module's integer-valued 40x40 test matrices), the rounding decides which IDAMAX picks: the reference itself returns IPIV(13) = 18 with LWORK = 5000 and 39 with LWORK = 2*N on that matrix (checked by compiling the reference), as the JS does. The factor A agrees to rounding; the module's tests check the factor at the minimum WORK against the optimum (ticket 0100).
